summary: Ronnenberg (Region Hannover) has no paid on-street parking regime that could be found: its published list of local statutes shows no parking-fee, resident-parking or parking-space (Stellplatz) statute, though this is only an absence in a list. Old council minutes mention parking-disc rules in places such as Bröhnstraße in Weetzen (not yet signed in January 2020) and Nenndorfer Straße (June 2021), and current signs and times are not verified. In September or October 2025 the administration said parking is checked by six marginally employed staff giving about 50 hours a week, with fines handled by the Region Hannover, and that the duty to provide parking spaces for dwellings no longer applies to building applications submitted after 30 June 2024. The main public car parks are free park-and-ride lots (the Hannover portal says all GVH park-and-ride sites are free): DB lists 197 spaces at Weetzen (the Region said 196 in 2021), and the Region's Infra said the 80-space lot at the Empelde Stadtbahn terminus was mostly full in 2024, with a 70-space lot opened on the Hannover side of the border on 20 March 2024. The Region's 2020 transport plan gave Weetzen P+R high priority and listed its extension as completed in 2019, and noted that fees might follow in future. The Region decided in November 2024 to extend bus line 500 to Weetzen station as a three-year trial, which in the third quarter of 2025 saw 770 boardings per weekday at the station stop across three lines. Stadtmobil has three cars in Empelde including one at the Empelde P+R since April 2025, and the city counts 45 public charge points at 17 sites, including 22 kW points at the three P+R sites; EnBW has run four fast chargers at Chemnitzer Straße since February 2024.

items.text: At the Weetzen local council meeting of 20 January 2020, the local mayor reported that no traffic signs had yet been put up for the parking-bay section of Bröhnstraße, so the rule of time-limited parking with a parking disc between 8:00 and 18:00 had not yet come into force there; the administration was to look into it. The page does not show whether the signs were installed later.
items.source_title: Ortsrat Weetzen, 20.01.2020, TOP 3.1 Bericht des Ortsbürgermeisters (Wortprotokoll)

items.text: In June 2021 residents told the council that many cars park without a parking disc on Nenndorfer Straße and side streets (Bruchstraße, Kopernikusstraße, Härkenstraße); the mayor said the city knew and was checking more often there, and was examining a temporary parking ban on street-sweeping days.
items.source_title: Rat der Stadt Ronnenberg, 21.06.2021, TOP 9 Einwohnerfragestunde (Wortprotokoll)

items.text: In a reply to a council inquiry of 17 September 2025, the mayor said parking enforcement is done by six marginally employed staff giving about 50 hours a week, that fines are processed by the Region Hannover, and that the aim of enforcement is traffic education, not maximum revenue.
items.source_title: Beantwortung der Anfrage AF/0067/2025/01 (Park- und Verkehrssituation Mesterwinkel), Ratsinformationssystem

items.text: In its reply to the AfD group's inquiry (17 September 2025), the administration explained that under the Lower Saxony building code (NBauO para 47) parking spaces no longer have to be provided for dwellings if the building application was submitted after 30 June 2024, with a transitional rule that required spaces removed after 18 March 2025 must be restored from 1 July 2025. It said that checking the building permits of the 129 plots in the Mesterwinkel area would take disproportionate effort and that, given the changed law, it could not be established whether an unlawful situation exists; it would examine individual plots if concrete violations were reported.
items.source_title: Beantwortung der Anfrage AF/0067/2025/01 (Park- und Verkehrssituation Mesterwinkel), Ratsinformationssystem

items.text: At an expert meeting on mobility for the town development concept (ISEK) on 21 July 2015, the administration said building permits normally required 2 parking spaces per dwelling, and noted that garages are often used as storerooms so cars end up in the street. The consultants' opening presentation of weaknesses, based on their analysis and earlier local events, included missing short-term and pick-up parking at the Empelde Stadtbahn loop and station.
items.source_title: ISEK Zukunftsdialog 2030: Expertengespräch Mobilität und Verkehr, 21.07.2015

items.text: The DB station page (read on 21 October 2026) lists the open P+R Weetzen Bahnhof car park at An den Kleingärten with 197 spaces, open 24 hours every day including public holidays; it lists no tariff.
The Hannover city page on parking (read on 21 October 2026) says all park-and-ride sites in the GVH area, about 6,100 car spaces in total, can be used free of charge and are open around the clock.

The Region Hannover's local transport plan 2020 (PDF created April 2020; the text does not say whether this is the adopted version) said that use of bike-and-ride and park-and-ride sites was currently free, that this could change in future, and that fees might make sense for spontaneous users of bike garages and for users of multi-storey car parks. It rated the Weetzen P+R as category 1 (high priority) and the Empelde Stadtbahn P+R as category 1, while the Ronnenberg and Empelde S-Bahn stations were category 3. The plan lists the Weetzen P+R extension as completed in 2019.

In May 2021 the Region Hannover said it digitally records occupancy at five pilot park-and-ride sites, including Weetzen with 196 spaces, and uses the traffic management centre (VMZ) to route drivers to free spaces via a navigation app.
items.source_title: Noch Platz für mein Auto (Region Hannover, 4 May 2021)

items.text: In its June 2022 comments on the Region's transport development plan VEP 2035+, Ronnenberg said an extension of the park-and-ride lots at Weetzen and Linderte/Holtensen should be examined, noting the Region's utilisation studies gave low priority to more P+R in the town. The city also asked for roofed, lockable bike parking at Weetzen and Empelde and for solar roofs and e-car charging at P+R sites.
items.source_title: Stellungnahme der Stadt Ronnenberg zum VEP 2035+ (VO/0563/2022)

items.text: In a circular to councillors after the 4 April 2018 committee meeting on the planned Hermann-Ehlers-Allee Stadtbahn platform and P+R lot on the Hannover side of the border, the administration restated the city's reservations (traffic effects on Berliner Straße, access from all directions, unclear user origins). It noted that the requested origin survey at the existing P+R at the Empelde loop had still not been done. According to the committee briefing, users of the new lot were expected mainly from the B 65 and the south-west, so no significant relief of the existing P+R lot and nearby housing was expected.
items.source_title: Ratsrundschreiben RR/230/2018: Hochbahnsteig und P+R Hermann-Ehlers-Allee

items.text: The Region's Infra said the 70-space park-and-ride at Hermann-Ehlers-Allee (Hannover-Badenstedt, on the border with Ronnenberg-Empelde, line 9) opened on 20 March 2024 with a sensor in every space showing live occupancy online. This is a Hannover site, context for Empelde.

In 2024 the Infra said the 80-space park-and-ride at the Empelde terminus of Stadtbahn line 9 was mostly completely occupied, while the new Badenstedt lot was used hesitantly at first, and asked drivers from Gehrden, Barsinghausen or Bad Nenndorf to use Badenstedt when Empelde is full.

The Region Hannover said on 7 November 2025 that it had decided in November 2024, for the 2025 timetable change, to extend the sprintH line 500 from Gehrden to Weetzen station as an initial three-year trial. Line 500 runs every 10 minutes Monday to Friday 6:00-19:00. An average of 770 passengers per weekday boarded at the stop Weetzen/Bahnhof/Westseite on lines 500, 520 and 522 together in the third quarter of 2025, up 12 percent from the second quarter.
items.source_title: Erfolgreicher Verkehrsversuch durch Verlängerung der Linie 500 (Region Hannover, 7 Nov 2025)

items.text: The city's car-sharing page (read on 21 October 2026) says stadtmobil Hannover has served Ronnenberg since 2021 and since April 2025 offers three cars in Empelde, including a petrol Ford Focus at the P+R car park Auf dem Rade at the line 9 terminus.

The city's charging page (read on 21 October 2026) reports 45 public charge points with 3,938 kW at 17 sites, after eight more high-power chargers opened in November 2025 at the retail car parks at Berliner Straße 23. It lists 22 kW points at the P+R sites Empelde (Auf dem Rade 3), Ronnenberg station (Benther Straße) and Weetzen station (Am Steinkamp 1).

In a statement for the planning committee of 19 November 2025, the administration said EnBW has operated four fast chargers (one 300 kW, three 150 kW) on 8 leased spaces at the Chemnitzer Straße retail centre since February 2024, and advised against a pilot solar roof there (cost about 120,000 euros, retail-centre owner Edeka sees no economic case). The centre has over 300 private spaces.
items.source_title: Stellungnahme zum Antrag Photovoltaik-Überdachungen von Ladestationen (AN/0245/2025/01)

gaps: No Ronnenberg paid-parking, resident-parking or Stellplatzsatzung document found (statute list at https://www.ronnenberg.de/service/satzungen-und-verordnungen/ shows none); the Parkscheibe areas (Bröhnstraße, Nenndorfer Straße) are known only from 2019-2021 council minutes, current signs and times not verified.

Region Hannover Nahverkehrsplan 2021 final PDF (https://www.lnvg.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Region_Hannover_-_NVP_2021_Internet.pdf) returned an HTML page instead of a PDF; the April 2020 plan version on hannover.de was used instead, so the final priorities may differ.

Weetzen P+R capacity differs by source (DB 197, Region 2021 196, a listing portal not used 273); no current count or utilisation statement by the city found, and no completed extension date beyond the Region's '2019 completed' note.
No Ronnenberg-specific parking guidance or open-data system, no council decision on Empelde centre parking, and no local press articles (HAZ, Calenberger Zeitung) were opened or searched in depth.
The Bürgerversammlung minutes (2019) and the Weetzen charging motion (2022) are short council documents; the motion's attachment text was not read.
EnBW press release on the 2024 Ronnenberg fast-charging site (enbw.com PDF) and the Region's line 500 2024 decision release were not opened.
